ei.title: 4번: The Two Faces of Negative Pressure
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: "Negative pressure" refers to a situation in which the pressure of an enclosed area is lower than that of the surrounding area. If the barrier between these two areas breaks, any substances in the high-pressure area will immediately flow into the low-pressure area. For example, undersea pipes used to transport oil are in a state of negative pressure; therefore, any break in the pipeline will cause it to fill with ocean water. This is much better than the opposite scenario, in which oil would be released into the ocean. However, negative pressure is not always beneficial, such as in the case of pipes carrying drinking water to a city. If these municipal waterlines are damaged, they can potentially suck in contaminated groundwater, which would then enter the water supply. For this reason, a system of gauges and valves is used to adjust and control their pressure.

det.korean: ① transport=수송하다 ② better → worse: 바닷물 유입이 기름 유출보다 '더 나은(better)' 상황이라 worse는 부적절 ←정답 ③ beneficial=유익한 ④ adjust=조절하다

det.korean: ① surrounding=주위의 ② released=방출된 ③ suck in → push out: 손상된 수도관은 오염된 지하수를 '빨아들이므로(suck in)' push out(밀어내다)은 부적절 ←정답 ④ adjust=조절하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: harmful=해로운 / predictable=예측 가능한 / artificial=인공적인 / beneficial=이로운
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 However(그러나)로 흐름이 바뀐다. 앞에서는 음압이 이로운 사례(해저 송유관 — 파손돼도 바닷물만 들어옴)를 들었고, 빈칸 뒤에는 도시 상수도관(손상 시 오염된 지하수를 빨아들임) 같은 '나쁜' 사례가 이어진다. 즉 '음압이 항상 ___인 것은 아니다' 뒤에 해로운 예가 오므로 빈칸은 '이로운(beneficial)'이어야 한다.
① harmful(해로운): 뒤에 해로운 예가 나오므로 'not always harmful'이면 문맥이 반대가 됨 — 부적절
② predictable(예측 가능한): 예측 가능성은 본문 논점이 아님 — 부적절
③ artificial(인공적인): 인공성은 언급되지 않음 — 부적절
④ beneficial(이로운): 이로운 사례 뒤 However로 해로운 사례를 도입 → not always beneficial ←정답
det.tip: However 뒤에 나쁜 예 → 앞은 '항상 이롭지(beneficial)는 않다'

det.korean: ② 'undersea pipes ... are in a state of negative pressure; any break ... will cause it to fill with ocean water' — 일치

det.tip: 해저 송유관 파손 → 바닷물 유입(negative pressure)

questions.passage: "Negative pressure" ①<u>refer</u> to a situation in which the pressure of an enclosed area is lower than that of the surrounding area. If the barrier between these two areas ②<u>breaks</u>, any substances in the high-pressure area will immediately flow into the low-pressure area. For example, undersea pipes used to transport oil are in a state of negative pressure; therefore, any break in the pipeline will cause it to fill with ocean water. This is much better than the opposite scenario, in which oil would be ③<u>released</u> into the ocean. However, negative pressure is not always beneficial, such as in the case of pipes carrying drinking water to a city. If these municipal waterlines are ④<u>damaged</u>, they can potentially suck in contaminated groundwater, which would then enter the water supply. For this reason, a system of gauges and valves is used to adjust and control their pressure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

det.analysis:
① refer: 'Negative pressure ___ to a situation' 주어 Negative pressure(단수)이므로 3인칭 단수 refers가 맞음. refer는 수일치 오류 ←정답
② breaks: 'If the barrier breaks' 조건절 현재시제 적절
③ released: 'oil would be released' would be + 과거분사 수동 적절
④ damaged: 'waterlines are damaged' be + 과거분사 수동 적절
det.tip: 단수 주어 Negative pressure → refers (refer 아님)
